# Gramlot 0.3.6 — Common server API and one request per Source node

This release is the review of the 0.3.5 releases. It changes the contract between the core and the server adapters, the rules of the calls a page makes, and the packaging of the Python package.

Use it with gramlot-py-server 0.2.11 and gramlot-js-server 0.2.14, and with the gramlot-examples gallery 0.3.9. Their lessons match this core: no base theme line, no empty `Logic`.

For page authors:

- The method of `remote`, `dataRpc`, `dataRemote` and `remoteSource` is `"method"` or `"a.b.c.method"`, resolved from the page. `remote` also accepts a `^` or `=` pointer for the name. An empty, null or malformed name rejects the call when it is sent.
- Each Source node has one request in flight, and its answer is always applied. A change during the flight waits with its parameters and is sent when the answer arrives. Removing the node, closing the page and the `dataRpc` timeout abort the call. `_onCalling` runs before a call of `remote`, `dataRpc` and `dataRemote`, and a `false` result makes no call.
- `Logic` is optional. A logic module without it has no logic methods.
- `dataRemote` reads synchronously by default (`sync=True`) on a transport that sends synchronous calls (HTTP). On the serverless Worker the read stays asynchronous. `gramlot.rpc.callSync` is the synchronous call from code.
- A control writes to Data only through a plain `^` pointer, one without a transform (`:` or `:=`), and a value equal to the Data is not written.
- `==` has one compile path: the text is trimmed, and a final `;` is accepted.
- `:=` expressions on SVG nodes, and on HTML nodes inside SVG, are computed by the page builder.
- After a change of a `^` argument, the first explicit read of a `dataRemote` makes no extra synchronous call.
- A JavaScript page module imports `Bag`, `BagNode` and `createDecimal` from `@gramlot/gramlot/page`, on the server and in the browser.
- Every page loads the base theme `gramlot-base` first, so a page does not need to list it in `css`. `css_theme` (`cssTheme` in JavaScript) of the page or of the server chooses another theme, or none with `False` (`false`). The base theme has the classes `.actions` and `.eyebrow`.
- The public documentation states that a style shortcut takes its CSS unit (`width="12rem"`, `margin_top="4px"`). A number becomes pixels only in `rounded` and its side and corner forms, `transform_translate_x`, `transform_translate_y` and `filter_blur`, in Python and JavaScript alike. No renderer code changed.
- The public documentation has a Server protocol page, and Writing pages is split into Data binding and controllers, Calling the server, and Remote content and lazy Data.

For adapter authors, in Python and JavaScript:

- `GramlotServer` provides the operations every adapter needs: `decode_body`, `call`, `close`, `open_page`, `close_all` and `theme_file` (JavaScript `decodeBody`, `call`, `close`, `openPage` or `registerPage`, `closeAll`, `themeFile`), and `companion_file` (`companionFile`) on `GramlotFileServer`. `decode_body` removes a leading byte order mark. The reference adapters keep only HTTP.
- `evaluate_auth` (`evaluateAuth`) receives the `identity` of the call.
- A page expires `page_ttl` seconds after its last use. Opening it and every call that names it for its owner renew the expiry. `GramlotServer.call` does it, and an adapter does nothing for it.
- `theme_file` (`themeFile`) is on `GramlotServer`, so every server serves the base theme its pages list.
- The server declares the syntax of method names in the bootstrap as `nameSyntax`. The core default is `NAME_SYNTAX`.
- A server can name a browser module in `serverAdapter`. Its default export is a `ServerAdapter` class that creates the transport. The transport provides `call`, `close` and `dispose`.
- The conformance check also verifies: `HEAD`, `PUT`, `DELETE` and `PATCH` on the page path answer 405 with `Allow: GET`; owner isolation; a leading byte order mark on `rpc` and `close`; `nameSyntax`; and, when given `page_ttl` (`pageTtl`), the renewal and the expiry of a page. Adapters published before this release, gramlot-py-server 0.2.10 and gramlot-js-server 0.2.13, fail some of these checks.

Packaging:

- The Python package is built with hatchling from the `src/` layout. It ships `py.typed` and declares the Apache-2.0 license with LICENSE and NOTICE. `setup.py` and `MANIFEST.in` are removed. A build without the browser runtime files stops with the same message as before, for the wheel, the sdist and the editable install.
- `scripts/install_js_artifacts.py` accepts the declared `@genrojs/*` dependencies. It refused all of them before.
- The JavaScript and JSR packages require `@genrojs/tytx` 0.16.3, which provides `getDateType`.

Verified with 3,651 JavaScript tests and 215 Python tests plus 382 subtests (one existing expected failure) on the release branch.
